title: Emphasize without changing the original
prompt: Label is a class with one property, Text, that any code can change. Complete Labels.Emphasize so it returns a new Label whose text is the original text followed by "!". The label passed in must still have its old text afterwards, and the result must be a different object.
hints: After Label copy = label; how many Label objects are there?
Assigning a class variable copies the reference. Only new creates another object.
Return new Label(label.Text + "!") and do not assign to label.Text.
checkLabels: The result's text must be the original text followed by "!".
The label passed in must keep its old text.
The result must be a new object, not the label passed in.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Changes the label that was passed in and returns it.
Expects assignment to copy the object.

feedback: Count the Label objects your method creates. If it never uses new, the result and the original are the same object.
